description: Outline planning permission for demolition of vacant residential care home and erection of a new 80-bed residential care home with associated bins and cycle provision. Re-siting of accesses (Landscaping Matter Reserved)
decision_conditions: Application for approval of the reserved matters shall be made to the Local Planning Authority before the expiration of three years from the date of this permission. The development hereby permitted shall be begun before the expiration of two years from the date of approval of the last of the reserved matters to be approved.Reason: To comply with Section 92 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990, as amended.

The premises shall be used only as an 80-bed residential care home within Use Class C2 of the Town and Country Planning (Use Classes) Order 1987, as amended, and for no other purpose within Use Class C2 or any other use class. Reason: To ensure that the development is occupied and operated in the manner assessed by the Local Planning Authority and to safeguard the living conditions of neighbouring occupiers, highway safety, parking conditions and the provision of specialist care accommodation.

No development, including demolition or site clearance, shall commence until a Construction Management Plan has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The approved Construction Management Plan shall be adhered to throughout the demolition and construction period. The Construction Management Plan shall include details of: a) how the development will be constructed; b) hours of working, which shall be limited to 08:00 to 18:00 Mondays to Fridays, 08:00 to 13:00 on Saturdays, and no working on Sundays, Bank Holidays or Public Holidays; c) the procedure for loading and unloading materials; d) construction traffic routing to and from the site; e) management of deliveries and collections, including the management of vehicles waiting to access the site; f) any reversing manoeuvres onto or from the public highway and the provision of banksmen; g) temporary site access arrangements; h) signage for construction traffic; i) temporary warning signs on adjacent roads, where required; j) anticipated statutory undertaker connections; k) storage of plant, materials and contractors' vehicles; l) parking of vehicles of site operatives and visitors; m) location of site compounds, cabins and welfare facilities; n) means of site enclosure and maintenance of hoardings; o) wheel washing facilities; p) measures for dust suppression, noise reduction and control of other nuisance; q) measures to protect pedestrian and highway safety;r) arrangements for recycling and disposing of demolition and construction waste; and s) arrangements for compliance with the Low Emission Zone and Non-Road Mobile Machinery requirements, where applicable. Reason: To safeguard the living conditions of neighbouring occupiers and the safety and operation of the highway network, in accordance with Policies T4 and T7 of the London Plan 2021 and Policies CS7, DM9 and DM10 of the LDF Core Strategy 2012. This condition is required to be pre-commencement because demolition and construction works could otherwise give rise to unacceptable impacts before mitigation has been agreed.

No development, including demolition or site clearance, shall commence until a detailed Construction Logistics Plan has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The Construction Logistics Plan shall be prepared in accordance with relevant TfL guidance and shall include details of construction vehicle routing, vehicle types, delivery booking systems, loading arrangements, pedestrian and cyclist safety measures, and measures to minimise vehicle movements and emissions. The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved Construction Logistics Plan. Reason: To ensure that construction traffic is appropriately managed, to minimise impacts on the highway network, and to promote safe and sustainable construction logistics, in accordance with Policies T1, T4 and T7 of the London Plan 2021. This condition is required to be pre-commencement because construction movements would occur from the outset of development.

No development, including demolition or site clearance, shall commence until a Dust Management Plan has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The Dust Management Plan shall include measures for monitoring and controlling dust deposition, dust flux, real-time PM10 monitoring and/or visual inspections, as appropriate. The Dust Management Plan shall incorporate the construction phase mitigation measures set out in the submitted Air Quality Assessment and shall comply with the GLA Control of Dust and Emissions during Construction and Demolition SPG, or any subsequent replacement guidance. The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved Dust Management Plan.Reason: To safeguard air quality and the living conditions of neighbouring occupiers during demolition and construction, in accordance with Policy SI1 of the London Plan 2021 and Policies DM9 and DM10 of the LDF Core Strategy 2012. This condition is required to be pre-commencement because demolition and construction works could give rise to dust and air quality impacts from the outset.

All Non-Road Mobile Machinery of net power between 37kW and 560kW used during demolition, site preparation and construction shall comply with the emission standards set out in the GLA Control of Dust and Emissions during Construction and Demolition SPG, or any subsequent replacement guidance. No Non-Road Mobile Machinery shall be used on site unless it complies with the relevant emission standards, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority. An up-to-date list of all Non-Road Mobile Machinery used on the site shall be maintained on the relevant online register. Reason: To safeguard air quality and minimise emissions during demolition and construction, in accordance with Policy SI1 of the London Plan 2021.

No development, including demolition or site clearance, shall commence until a Phase 1 Preliminary Risk Assessment has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The assessment shall include a desktop study, site walkover, identification of previous uses, potential contaminants, potential contaminant sources, pathways and receptors, and a conceptual site model. Where the Phase 1 Preliminary Risk Assessment identifies no unacceptable risk, no further contaminated land investigation shall be required unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Reason: To ensure that the site is suitably investigated and to prevent harm to human health, controlled waters and the wider environment, having regard to the site's previous industrial history. This condition is required to be pre-commencement because contamination risks must be understood before works disturb the ground.

Where the approved Phase 1 Preliminary Risk Assessment identifies potential contamination risks, no development, except demolition to slab level, shall commence until a Phase 2 Site Investigation and Risk Assessment has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The investigation shall be undertaken by a suitably qualified person and shall identify the nature and extent of contamination, assess risks to all relevant receptors, and determine whether remediation is required. Reason: To ensure that contamination risks are properly assessed before development proceeds and to prevent harm to human health, controlled waters and the wider environment.

Where the approved Phase 2 Site Investigation identifies unacceptable risks from contamination, no development, except demolition to slab level and site investigation works, shall commence until a Remediation Strategy has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The Remediation Strategy shall include remediation objectives, the remediation methodology, implementation timetable, verification requirements and any long-term monitoring or maintenance measures. The development shall thereafter be carried out in accordance with the approved Remediation Strategy. Reason: To ensure that the site is remediated to a standard suitable for the approved use and to protect future occupiers, neighbouring land and the environment.

No part of the development shall be occupied until any approved remediation works have been completed and a Verification Report has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The Verification Report shall demonstrate that the remediation works have been carried out in accordance with the approved Remediation Strategy and shall include the results of verification sampling, details of imported materials, details of materials removed from the site, and confirmation that the site is suitable for the approved use. Reason: To ensure that remediation has been satisfactorily completed before occupation and that the site is safe for future occupiers.

If, during development, contamination is encountered which has not previously been identified, development in the affected area shall cease until the contamination has been assessed and a remediation strategy has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The approved remediation strategy shall be implemented in full before development in the affected area resumes. Reason: To ensure that any unexpected contamination is appropriately managed and to protect human health, controlled waters and the wider environment.

All hard surfaced areas shall be constructed using permeable or porous materials, or shall be designed to direct run-off water to a permeable or porous area or surface within the site. The approved hard surfacing shall be installed before first occupation and retained thereafter. Reason: To reduce surface water run-off and flood risk, in accordance with Policy SI13 of the London Plan 2021 and Policy DM4 of the LDF Core Strategy 2012.

No development, including demolition or site clearance, shall commence until a detailed surface water drainage strategy has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, in consultation with the Lead Local Flood Authority. The strategy shall include: a) details of the drainage hierarchy and evidence that priority has been given to infiltration and gravity drainage where feasible; b) calculations demonstrating surface water storage, attenuation and discharge rates for all relevant storm events, including climate change allowance; c) details of all proposed SuDS features, including location, dimensions, levels, construction details and exceedance flow routes; d) details of permeable paving, green roofs, rain gardens, swales, detention basins or other SuDS features, where proposed; e) where a pumped solution is proposed, a written justification demonstrating why gravity drainage is not reasonably practicable, together with details of pump capacity, backup measures and maintenance arrangements; and f) a management and maintenance plan for the lifetime of the development. The approved drainage strategy shall be implemented before first occupation and shall thereafter be retained and maintained in accordance with the approved details. Reason: To prevent increased flood risk on or off the site and to ensure the development incorporates sustainable drainage measures, in accordance with Policy SI13 of the London Plan 2021 and Policy DM4 of the LDF Core Strategy 2012. This condition is required to be pre-commencement because the drainage strategy may affect below-ground works, levels, attenuation, construction sequencing and site layout.

No development above ground level shall commence until details of all external facing materials have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The submitted details shall include: a) a full schedule of external materials and finishes; b) manufacturer specifications; c) brick type, bond, mortar colour, pointing profile and jointing; d) render, cladding, stonework or other facing materials; e) ventilation bricks, grilles, drainage goods and external metalwork; f) window and door materials and finishes; g) balcony, balustrade and privacy screen materials; h) boundary treatments, gates and fencing; i) coded and annotated elevations showing where each material is to be used; and j) a physical sample panel or mock-up of the proposed external wall construction. The sample panel shall be constructed at 1:1 scale, shall be at least 2 square metres in area unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority, and shall include representative examples of brickwork, mortar, pointing, window reveals and any material junctions. The sample panel shall be retained on site for inspection until the relevant external works are substantially complete. The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details. Reason: To ensure a high-quality appearance and to safeguard the character and appearance of the surrounding area, in accordance with Policy D3 of the London Plan 2021 and Policies CS8 and DM10 of the LDF Core Strategy 2012.

No development above ground level shall commence until detailed drawings of all external windows and doors have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The details shall include elevations, plans and sections at a scale of 1:10 or 1:20, together with details of materials, colour, opening methods, reveals, cills, heads and surrounds. The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details and retained thereafter. Reason: To ensure a high-quality detailed design and satisfactory appearance, in accordance with Policy D3 of the London Plan 2021 and Policies CS8 and DM10 of the LDF Core Strategy 2012.

No development above ground level shall commence until full details of the roof design, roof materials, rooftop plant, plant enclosures and plant screening have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The details shall include the location, height, appearance, materials, acoustic performance and visual screening of any rooftop plant or equipment. The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details and retained thereafter. Reason: To safeguard the character and appearance of the area, the living conditions of neighbouring occupiers and the appearance of the completed development, in accordance with Policies D3 and D14 of the London Plan 2021 and Policies CS8 and DM10 of the LDF Core Strategy 2012.

No development above ground level shall commence until a detailed boundary treatment plan has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The plan shall identify all existing and proposed boundary treatments, including walls, fences, railings, gates and retaining structures, together with their height, materials, design and location. The approved boundary treatments shall be installed before first occupation and retained thereafter. Reason: To ensure a satisfactory appearance, protect neighbouring amenity, provide appropriate site security and ensure an acceptable relationship with adjoining land, in accordance with Policy D3 of the London Plan 2021 and Policies CS8 and DM10 of the LDF Core Strategy 2012.

No external lighting shall be installed until a detailed external lighting scheme has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The scheme shall include the location, type, specification, intensity, beam orientation, hours of operation and light spill of all external lighting. The lighting shall be designed to minimise glare, light spill beyond the site boundaries and upward light spill. The approved lighting shall be installed and maintained in accordance with the approved details. Reason: To safeguard the living conditions of neighbouring occupiers, highway safety and biodiversity, in accordance with Policies D3 and G6 of the London Plan 2021 and Policies CS3, DM6 and DM10 of the LDF Core Strategy 2012.

No development above ground level shall commence until detailed drawings and specifications have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority demonstrating that the resident bedrooms, communal facilities, circulation spaces and associated external areas provide an accessible environment for wheelchair users and people with impaired mobility. The approved details shall demonstrate, where relevant, step-free access, accessible sanitary facilities, lifts, corridor widths, door clearances and wheelchair manoeuvring spaces, having regard to Approved Document M Volume 2. The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details and retained thereafter. Reason: To secure an inclusive development that is accessible to all users, including older people and disabled people, in accordance with Policy D5 of the London Plan 2021 and Policy DM10 of the LDF Core Strategy 2012.

Before first occupation, the windows on the side and rear elevations shown on drawing nos. BR-AP6-120 and BR-AP6-117 shall be fitted with obscure glazing to a minimum of level 3 on the standard scale where the window is less than 1.7 metres above finished floor level. No part of those windows below 1.7 metres above finished floor level shall be openable. The obscure glazing and restricted opening arrangements shall be retained thereafter. Reason: To safeguard the privacy and living conditions of neighbouring occupiers, in accordance with Policy D3 of the London Plan 2021 and Policy DM10 of the LDF Core Strategy 2012.

Before first occupation, privacy screens measuring 1.7 metres in height from finished floor level shall be installed to the balconies on the side and rear elevations shown on drawing no. BR-AP6-120. The screens shall be obscure glazed to a minimum of level 3 on the standard scale, or shall be of another design first approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The privacy screens shall be retained thereafter. Reason: To safeguard the privacy and living conditions of neighbouring occupiers, in accordance with Policy D3 of the London Plan 2021 and Policy DM10 of the LDF Core Strategy 2012.

No flat roof area shall be used as a balcony, terrace, sitting-out area or amenity space unless expressly shown as such on the approved plans. Access to all other flat roof areas shall be for maintenance or emergency purposes only. Reason: To safeguard the privacy and living conditions of neighbouring occupiers, in accordance with Policy D3 of the London Plan 2021 and Policy DM10 of the LDF Core Strategy 2012.

Any application for approval of landscaping Reserved Matters shall include: a) hard and soft landscaping details; b) planting plans, including species, size, density and location of planting; c) tree planting and replacement tree details; d) boundary treatments; e) external amenity areas; f) secure walking routes and external spaces for residents; g) street furniture, including benches, litter bins, bollards and signage; h) lighting integrated with the landscape scheme; i) biodiversity and urban greening measures; j) landscape maintenance and management arrangements; and k) a timetable for implementation. The approved landscaping shall be implemented in accordance with the approved timetable. Any trees or plants which die, are removed, or become seriously damaged or diseased within five years of planting shall be replaced in the next planting season with others of similar size and species, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Reason: To ensure a high-quality landscape setting, safeguard the character and appearance of the area, enhance biodiversity and provide appropriate external amenity space for future residents, in accordance with Policies D3, D5, G5 and G6 of the London Plan 2021 and Policies CS8, DM6 and DM10 of the LDF Core Strategy 2012.

The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved Arboricultural Impact Assessment, Arboricultural Method Statement and Tree Protection Plan dated 13 November 2025. The approved tree protection measures shall be installed before any works commence on site and shall be retained for the duration of demolition and construction works. Reason: To protect retained trees and safeguard the character and appearance of the area, in accordance with Policy G7 of the London Plan 2021 and Policies CS8 and DM10 of the LDF Core Strategy 2012.

The development hereby approved shall achieve a minimum Urban Greening Factor of 0.49, as set out in the submitted Urban Greening Factor Assessment. The approved urban greening measures shall be implemented before first occupation and shall be retained and maintained thereafter. Reason: To secure appropriate urban greening and environmental enhancement, in accordance with Policy G5 of the London Plan 2021 and Policies CS3 and DM6 of the LDF Core Strategy 2012.

Prior to occupation of the development hereby approved, a Biodiversity Gain Plan shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The Biodiversity Gain Plan shall include: a) information about the steps taken or to be taken to minimise adverse effects of the development on onsite habitat and any other habitat; b) the pre-development biodiversity value of the onsite habitat; c) the post-development biodiversity value of the onsite habitat; d) any registered offsite biodiversity gain allocated to the development and its biodiversity value; e) any biodiversity credits purchased for the development; and f) any other matters required by relevant regulations. In the first instance, the applicant shall explore the provision of any required off-site biodiversity net gain within the immediate locality of the site. Reason: To ensure the development delivers biodiversity net gain in accordance with Schedule 7A of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.

Prior to commencement of development, excluding demolition, a Habitat Management and Monitoring Plan shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The Habitat Management and Monitoring Plan shall be prepared in accordance with the approved Biodiversity Gain Plan and shall include: a) a non-technical summary; b) roles and responsibilities for delivery; c) habitat creation and enhancement works; d) management measures for a period of 30 years from completion of development; and e) monitoring methodology, frequency and reporting arrangements. The development shall thereafter be carried out in accordance with the approved Habitat Management and Monitoring Plan. Reason: To ensure the delivery, management and monitoring of biodiversity net gain in accordance with Schedule 7A of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.

The development shall not be occupied until the habitat creation and enhancement works set out in the approved Habitat Management and Monitoring Plan have been completed and a completion report has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The created and/or enhanced habitat shall thereafter be managed and maintained in accordance with the approved Habitat Management and Monitoring Plan. Reason: To ensure the delivery and long-term maintenance of biodiversity net gain in accordance with Schedule 7A of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.

A minimum of three swift bricks shall be incorporated into the external walls of the development before first occupation. The swift bricks shall be retained thereafter. Reason: To enhance biodiversity, in accordance with the Kingston Swift Species Action Plan 2023, Policy DM6 of the LDF Core Strategy 2012 and Policy G6 of the London Plan 2021.

Before first occupation, full details of the cycle parking facilities shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The details shall include: a) the number of long-stay and short-stay cycle spaces; b) confirmation of expected staff numbers and evidence of compliance with London Plan Policy T5; c) provision for larger and adapted cycles, with at least 5% of spaces suitable for oversized cycles; d) details of access arrangements, including aisle widths and manoeuvring space; e) details of the location of cycle stores in relation to the site entrance; f) details of security, weather protection and lighting; and g) details of visitor cycle parking. The approved cycle parking shall be provided before first occupation and retained thereafter. Reason: To promote active travel and ensure suitable, accessible and secure cycle parking provision, in accordance with Policies T5, D3 and D5 of the London Plan 2021 and Policies CS6 and DM8 of the LDF Core Strategy 2012.

The car parking spaces shown on the approved plans, including the two blue badge spaces and operational/servicing bay, shall be provided before first occupation. The spaces shall be surfaced, drained, marked out and made available for use before first occupation and shall be retained thereafter for the parking and servicing needs of the development. Reason: To ensure appropriate parking and servicing provision in the interests of highway safety and accessibility, in accordance with Policies T4 and T6 of the London Plan 2021 and Policies CS7 and DM9 of the LDF Core Strategy 2012.

Before first occupation, details of electric vehicle charging infrastructure for the approved car parking and servicing spaces shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The approved electric vehicle charging infrastructure shall be installed before first occupation and retained thereafter. Reason: To reduce emissions and support sustainable transport, in accordance with Policies T6 and SI1 of the London Plan 2021.

No development above ground level shall commence until a detailed Delivery and Servicing Plan has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The Delivery and Servicing Plan shall include: a) servicing and delivery arrangements; b) loading and unloading locations; c) vehicle types and frequency of servicing; d) management of deliveries to avoid highway obstruction; e) arrangements for refuse collection; f) measures to minimise vehicle movements; g) measures to encourage low-emission or electric freight vehicles; and h) arrangements for monitoring and review. The development shall be operated in accordance with the approved Delivery and Servicing Plan. Reason: To ensure that deliveries and servicing are appropriately managed in the interests of highway safety, residential amenity and sustainable transport, in accordance with Policies T4 and T7 of the London Plan 2021 and Policies CS7 and DM9 of the LDF Core Strategy 2012.

Before first occupation, a detailed Travel Plan shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The Travel Plan shall include measures to encourage staff, visitors and residents to travel by sustainable modes and to discourage unnecessary car use and on-street parking. The Travel Plan shall include: a) appointment of a Travel Plan Coordinator; b) staff travel information and induction measures; c) visitor travel information; d) measures to encourage walking, cycling and public transport use; e) measures to discourage staff and visitors from parking on surrounding residential streets and nearby public car parks; f) monitoring targets; g) annual monitoring and review; and h) remedial measures if targets are not met. The approved Travel Plan shall be implemented from first occupation and retained thereafter. Reason: To promote sustainable travel, reduce car dependency and minimise parking impacts, in accordance with Policies T1, T4 and T6 of the London Plan 2021 and Policies CS6, CS7, DM8 and DM9 of the LDF Core Strategy 2012.

Before first occupation, a scheme of noise insulation and ventilation shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The scheme shall demonstrate that internal noise levels will not exceed: 35 dB LAeq, 16 hour in living rooms and bedrooms during the daytime, 07:00 to 23:00; and 30 dB LAeq, 8 hour and 45 dB LAFmax in bedrooms during the night-time, 23:00 to 07:00, in accordance with BS8233:2014. Where these levels cannot be achieved with windows open, appropriate acoustic ventilation shall be provided. The approved noise insulation and ventilation measures shall be installed before first occupation and retained thereafter. Reason: To ensure satisfactory living conditions for future residents, in accordance with Policy D14 of the London Plan 2021 and Policy DM10 of the LDF Core Strategy 2012.

The rating level of noise from fixed plant and equipment associated with the development shall be at least 5dB below the existing background noise level at the nearest noise-sensitive premises when assessed in accordance with BS4142:2014. Before any fixed plant is installed, details of the plant and a noise assessment demonstrating compliance with this requirement shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The plant shall be installed and operated in accordance with the approved details and retained thereafter. Reason: To safeguard the living conditions of neighbouring occupiers and future residents, in accordance with Policy D14 of the London Plan 2021 and Policy DM10 of the LDF Core Strategy 2012.

No development above ground level shall commence until details of security measures to minimise the risk of crime and meet the specific security needs of the development have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The details shall have regard to Secured by Design principles. The approved measures shall be implemented before first occupation and retained thereafter. Reason: To improve community safety and crime prevention, in accordance with Policy D11 of the London Plan 2021 and Policies CS14 and DM22 of the LDF Core Strategy 2012.

Before first occupation, a Secured by Design certificate, or equivalent written confirmation from a Designing Out Crime Officer, shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority. Reason: To confirm that the development has incorporated appropriate crime prevention measures, in accordance with Policy D11 of the London Plan 2021 and Policies CS14 and DM22 of the LDF Core Strategy 2012.

The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved Fire Plan, drawing no. BR-AP6-122, and the approved Fire Strategy. The approved fire safety measures shall be implemented before first occupation and retained thereafter. Reason: In the interests of fire safety and the safety of building users, in accordance with Policy D12 of the London Plan 2021.

The development hereby approved shall achieve a minimum 37.76% reduction in carbon emissions over Part L of the Building Regulations 2021, as set out in the submitted Energy and Sustainability Statement dated 19 November 2025. Before first occupation, evidence demonstrating that the required carbon reduction has been achieved shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The evidence shall include an assessment by a suitably qualified professional of the carbon reduction measures implemented within the development. The approved measures shall be retained and maintained for the lifetime of the development. Reason: To ensure that the development minimises carbon emissions and accords with the approved energy strategy, in accordance with Policy SI2 of the London Plan 2021 and Policies DM1 and DM3 of the LDF Core Strategy 2012.

No development above ground level shall commence until details of water efficiency measures have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details and the measures shall be retained thereafter. Reason: To minimise potable water consumption, in accordance with Policy SI5 of the London Plan 2021.

The refuse and recycling facilities shown on the approved plans shall be provided before first occupation and retained thereafter. The developer and/or operator shall ensure that all refuse and recyclable materials associated with the development are stored within the approved facilities or internally within the building, and that no refuse or recycling material is stored or placed on the public highway except on the day of collection. Reason: To ensure proper waste management and safeguard the character and appearance of the area and the living conditions of neighbouring occupiers, in accordance with Policy SI17 of the London Plan 2021 and Policies CS8 and DM10 of the LDF Core Strategy 2012.

No external signage shall be installed until details of the signage have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The details shall include the location, size, design, materials and any illumination, including hours of operation and brightness levels. The signage shall be installed only in accordance with the approved details and retained thereafter. Reason: To safeguard the character and appearance of the area and neighbouring amenity, in accordance with Policy D3 of the London Plan 2021 and Policies CS8 and DM10 of the LDF Core Strategy 2012.

Before first occupation, an Operational Management Plan for the care home shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The plan shall include details of: a) the nature of the care home operation; b) maximum bedspaces; c) staffing numbers and shift patterns; d) visitor management; e) servicing and delivery arrangements;f) emergency access arrangements; g) parking management; h) refuse management; i) arrangements for resident access to external amenity space; and j) a named site management contact for local residents and the Council. The care home shall operate in accordance with the approved Operational Management Plan. Reason: To ensure that the development operates in a manner compatible with neighbouring residential amenity, highway safety and the approved C2 use.
